clue.text: Oblong-shaped article found in city

indicators.note: shaped says the letters of oblong are moulded into a fresh form

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An oblong-shaped object turns up in some city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oblong-shaped' reads as one adjective, but the hyphen hides the anagram signal 'shaped'; the city is the Italian one, not a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Bologna is a city in northern Italy, capital of Emilia-Romagna.

clue.text: Drive away contents of vans, in error

indicators.note: in places the inside of vans within the slang word for error

parts.note: bish is British slang for a mistake or blunder

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inside letters, here of vans

explanation.surface: Get rid of what's in the vans because it was a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents of vans' gives AN, which goes 'in' BISH, a British slang word for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish is to expel or exile someone, sending them off.

clue.text: Underworld fellow I reformed

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters of fellow I are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A criminal says he has turned over a new leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' makes a gangster go straight in the surface; cryptically it rearranges FELLOW I.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowlife is the criminal class collectively, the underworld of society.

clue.text: Surprised expression — result of catching him young, according to Johnson?

definitions.text: result of catching him young, according to Johnson?

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise, and Dr Johnson's view on catching a man early.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Johnson said much may be made of a Scotchman if he be caught young, so the result is a fine figure of a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Good heavens!' is a cry of astonishment; Johnson's remark implies a Scotsman caught young becomes a distinguished man.

clue.text: Taken on board a ship? A limited arrangement

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: an arrangement sets the letters of A limited in a new order

explanation.surface: Was something taken on board a ship, under a restricted deal?
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges A LIMITED into IMILATED. 'Taken on board' sounds nautical, but means absorbed or understood.
explanation.definitionFit: To take an idea on board is to absorb and understand it fully.

clue.text: Island queen taking the air in the West Indies

definitions.text: the air in the West Indies

explanation.surface: A queen of some island enjoys a breath of Caribbean breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the air' looks like fresh air to breathe, but here it is a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer the nymph Calypso ruled the island Ogygia; a calypso is also the typical Trinidadian folk song, a West Indian melody.

clue.text: Keen pack

explanation.surface: An eager group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like an adjective, eager, but it is the verb to wail for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in grief; a pack of hounds is called a cry.

clue.text: Classify the foreign deity

parts.note: la is the French for the
Bel is a Babylonian god

explanation.surface: Categorise the alien god.
explanation.definitionFit: To label things is to tag them as belonging to a class or category.

clue.text: Fruit gathered in fall

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
met means assembled or gathered together

explanation.surface: Fruit was picked up during the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' is the American autumn in the surface, but here it is a verb for dropping sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: To plummet is to drop steeply and swiftly, a sudden fall.

clue.text: Crimes of dishonest dealers

parts.note: fences are people who deal in stolen goods

explanation.surface: Crimes committed by crooked traders.
explanation.definitionFit: Offences are breaches of law, crimes.

clue.text: Modern fabric's original state

parts.note: modern means new
jersey is a knitted fabric

explanation.surface: A new material's first condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original state' looks like a fabric's first condition, but means one of the thirteen founding states of the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: New Jersey was one of the thirteen colonies that became the first states of the American union.

clue.text: Bank's deception

explanation.surface: A bank's deceit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluff is a steep cliff or riverbank; to bluff is to deceive by a show of confidence, as in poker.

clue.text: Leader of sinners is, not commonly this!

definitions.text: Leader of sinners is, not commonly this!

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of sinners

parts.note: is not, in common or uneducated speech, is ain't

explanation.surface: Whoever leads sinners is not, as people say, a holy person.
explanation.walkthrough: S starts 'sinners', and AIN'T is the colloquial form of 'is not'. The whole clue is also the definition: the leader of the sinners is unlikely to be a holy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A holy, canonised person is about as far from a ringleader of sinners as can be, which the exclamation teases.

clue.text: King and Queen as intermediaries?

parts.note: on a chessboard the king and queen start on the two central squares of the back row, so they are the pieces in the centre; the definition is go-betweens

explanation.surface: A monarch and consort acting as go-betweens.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests royals brokering a deal; the cryptic reading is the chessboard, where king and queen begin in the central files.
explanation.definitionFit: Intermediaries are agents, dealers or brokers who stand between two parties.

clue.text: One page filled after record's beaten, perhaps

indicators.note: after puts the record's word ahead of the rest

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
I is the Roman numeral one
lined means filled inside, as a coat with a lining

explanation.surface: A single page got filled once a record was broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten, perhaps' looks like a broken record, but it is the definition: punished, and 'perhaps' shows beating is just one way.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disciplined has been punished, and a beating is one example of that punishment.

clue.text: Labourer with mallet does for insect

parts.note: Hercules of Greek myth performed twelve labours, so he is the labourer
a beetle is a heavy wooden mallet or rammer

explanation.surface: A worker with a mallet kills an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does for' looks like 'kills', but is just a link: the two pieces together make the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hercules beetle is a giant rhinoceros beetle of Central and South America.

clue.text: Ambassador upset about politician to an extent that produces stress

indicators.note: about says the reversed title goes around the politician
upset turns the ambassador's title over, reading it backwards

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
MP is a Member of Parliament
size is extent or magnitude

explanation.surface: An upset ambassador talks about a politician so much that it causes stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses HE to EH, which goes 'about' MP for EMPH; then A SIZE. The words 'to' and 'that produces' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise is to stress or give special weight to something.

clue.text: Like mirth, it's present in Clown's song

definitions.text: Like mirth, it's present in Clown's song

parts.words: Like mirth, it's present in Clown's song
parts.note: the Clown, Feste, sings in Twelfth Night that present mirth hath present something; the word that follows is the answer

explanation.surface: Something joyful features in a clown's ditty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Clown is Feste in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night; his song O Mistress Mine has the line 'Present mirth hath present laughter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirth and the sound of merriment go together, as the Shakespeare song pairs them.

clue.text: Girl turns to erotic entertainment as profitable enterprise

indicators.note: turns says the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Tessa is a girl's name
stripping is an erotic striptease act

explanation.surface: A young woman takes up stripping because it pays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses TESSA to make ASSET. The surface suggests a career change, but the definition is the money-making business of buying a company and selling off its parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Asset-stripping means buying a firm cheaply and selling its assets individually for gain, a lucrative if ruthless business.

clue.text: Argentine soil, nonetheless, sort of light

indicators.note: none less means without nothing, the round letter O shaped like a zero

parts.note: a Very light is a coloured signal flare

explanation.surface: Argentine earth is, all the same, some kind of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' is read as 'none less', so SOIL loses its O, giving SIL. 'Argentine' looks like Argentina but means of silver, from heraldic argent.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentine, from the Latin for silver, means silver-coloured or shining like silver.

clue.text: Sisters love, we hear, outlaw

indicators.note: we hear says the word for nothing is taken as heard

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, so none
hood is short for hoodlum, an outlaw

explanation.surface: Sisters love, people say, an outlaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is a zero score in tennis, so NONE, which sounds like NUN. Robin Hood also fits 'outlaw'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisters of a religious order collectively make up the community of women in convents.

clue.text: Continue to care for judge

parts.note: reck is an old word meaning to heed or care
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: Keep looking after the magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'judge' looks like a magistrate but is a verb, to estimate.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to calculate or estimate, so to judge.

clue.text: Fashion model glad to get top award

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters of model glad are reshaped

explanation.surface: A fashion model is pleased to win the top prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like part of 'fashion model', but it is a verb signalling the anagram of MODEL GLAD.
explanation.definitionFit: First place in Olympic and similar competitions earns a gold medal, the highest prize.

clue.text: Doctor raised rent for accommodation, by the way

parts.note: MO is a medical officer

indicators.note: raised means read upward in this down clue

parts.note: to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: The doctor put the rent up, incidentally, for lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses LET to TEL in a down entry. 'by the way' looks like 'incidentally', but means by the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: Roadside accommodation for motorists is a hotel built beside the highway.

clue.text: Maiden in the inn answered back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A girl at the pub replied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters EINNA inside 'the inn answered'; 'back' reverses them. The maiden is a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name stands for a maiden, as a crossword shows an example of a young woman.

clue.text: Nellie's flower

explanation.surface: A flower belonging to Nellie.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Nell, heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop, is Nell Trent. 'flower' is the crossword river, a thing that flows; the Trent is a major English river.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens gave Little Nell the family name Trent; a flower in crosswords is a river, and the Trent runs through the English Midlands.

clue.text: Creative result from man who toils till after one

indicators.note: after says the word for till comes behind the numeral one

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker
I is the Roman numeral one
to till land is to work it

explanation.surface: A creative result comes from a man who toils till after one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'till after one' looks like a time of day, but 'till' is the verb and 'after' places WORK behind I.
explanation.definitionFit: Handiwork is something made by one's own skill, a creative product.

clue.text: Attention-seeker in boat

explanation.surface: Someone shouting for notice from a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoy is an old call to attract attention; a hoy was also a small coastal sailing vessel.

clue.text: Payment for Henry IV, say?

explanation.surface: A fee paid to a king.
explanation.definitionFit: A royalty is a fee paid to an author or patent holder; a king such as Henry IV is a member of royalty, kings collectively.

clue.text: China's red revolution ends in disorder

indicators.note: revolution turns over the letters of red
in disorder jumbles the letters of ends

explanation.surface: China's red revolution finishes in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' turns RED into DRE and 'in disorder' turns ENDS into SDEN. 'China' looks like the country, but it is porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is a fine porcelain made at Meissen near the German city of that name.
